--- title: "Module 3 - Tutorial 1" subtitle: "SEC Chunk Retrieval Foundations" description: "Build a lightweight semantic retriever over SEC text to prepare for the retrieval-focused lab and assignment workflow." number-sections: true date: "2026-02-15" date-modified: today date-format: long engine: jupyter format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 code-overflow: wrap categories: ['Prompt Engineering', 'Tokenization', 'Embeddings', 'Semantic Search', 'Guided Implementation'] execute: echo: true eval: true warning: false message: false --- ## Module Learning Objectives By the end of Module 3, students should be able to: 1. explain how embeddings support retrieval over text corpora 2. build a simple retrieval layer over SEC chunks 3. inspect whether retrieved evidence is actually useful 4. prepare retrieval artifacts for later prompting and project work 5. connect retrieval to the attention idea of selecting relevant context ## Tutorial Learning Objectives By the end of this tutorial, you will: 1. Load a small SEC chunk corpus. 2. Embed those chunks. 3. Build a FAISS index. 4. Retrieve the top passages for analyst-style questions. 5. Inspect whether the retrieved evidence is actually useful. 6. Interpret similarity scores as a lightweight attention-like ranking over external text. ## How This Tutorial Connects - `M03_Lab1` extends this into more deliberate retrieval experiments. - `M03_Lab2` and `M03_A` build on the same evidence-first workflow. - `M03_Proj` can reuse the same retrieval design ideas in a larger product context. ## Conceptual Bridge: Retrieval as External Attention In the lecture, attention let a decoder focus on the source states most relevant to the current generated token. Retrieval-augmented generation uses a related systems idea: before asking a model to answer, we select the chunks most relevant to the user question. The analogy is not exact, but it is useful: | Neural attention | Retrieval workflow | |---|---| | query state $s_{t-1}$ | user question | | keys/values $h_j$ | embedded document chunks | | attention weights $\alpha_{jt}$ | similarity scores or ranked neighbors | | context vector $c_t$ | selected evidence placed in the prompt | In this tutorial, FAISS gives us a practical version of that selection step. ## Setup ::: {#7964bd76 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from pathlib import Path import pandas as pd import numpy as np import faiss from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer ``` ::: ## Step 1: Load SEC Chunks ::: {#f744ebf1 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} chunks_df = pd.read_csv("../deliverables-solutions/Assignments/outputs/M01_A_sol/chunks.csv") chunks_df = chunks_df[["chunk_id", "company", "item", "chunk_text"]].dropna().head(300) chunks_df.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
chunk_id company item chunk_text
0 MSFT_2020_7_1 Microsoft 7 Item 7 Productivity and Business Processes and...
1 MSFT_2020_7_2 Microsoft 7 These metrics provide strategic product insigh...
2 MSFT_2020_7_3 Microsoft 7 Refer to the Non-GAAP Financial Measures secti...
3 MSFT_2020_7_4 Microsoft 7 Productivity and Business Processes revenue in...
4 MSFT_2020_7_5 Microsoft 7 Gross margin percentage increased, driven by s...
``` ::: ::: ## Step 2: Embed the Corpus ::: {#846272cf .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} embedder = SentenceTransformer("all-MiniLM-L6-v2") embeddings = embedder.encode( chunks_df["chunk_text"].tolist(), batch_size=32, convert_to_numpy=True, normalize_embeddings=True ).astype("float32") embeddings.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (300, 384) ``` ::: ::: ## Step 3: Build the Index ::: {#ead5e6fc .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} index = faiss.IndexFlatIP(embeddings.shape[1]) index.add(embeddings) print("Indexed vectors:", index.ntotal) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Indexed vectors: 300 ``` ::: ::: ## Step 4: Retrieval Function ::: {#a88585de .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} def retrieve(query: str, k: int = 5) -> pd.DataFrame: q = embedder.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True).astype("float32") scores, idxs = index.search(q, k) rows = chunks_df.iloc[idxs[0]].copy() rows["score"] = scores[0] return rows[["chunk_id", "company", "item", "score", "chunk_text"]] ``` ::: ## Step 5: Test Queries ::: {#47f430b5 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} queries = [ "cybersecurity and data privacy risk", "supply chain disruption and vendor dependency", "regulatory uncertainty and litigation exposure", ] for q in queries: print("\\nQUERY:", q) print(retrieve(q, k=3)[["chunk_id", "company", "item", "score"]]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` \nQUERY: cybersecurity and data privacy risk chunk_id company item score 261 MSFT_2020_8_178 Microsoft 8 0.603349 216 MSFT_2020_8_133 Microsoft 8 0.593432 203 MSFT_2020_8_120 Microsoft 8 0.571941 \nQUERY: supply chain disruption and vendor dependency chunk_id company item score 236 MSFT_2020_8_153 Microsoft 8 0.582388 285 MSFT_2020_8_202 Microsoft 8 0.565023 127 MSFT_2020_8_44 Microsoft 8 0.544712 \nQUERY: regulatory uncertainty and litigation exposure chunk_id company item score 248 MSFT_2020_8_165 Microsoft 8 0.608994 245 MSFT_2020_8_162 Microsoft 8 0.545278 246 MSFT_2020_8_163 Microsoft 8 0.537888 ``` ::: ::: ## Step 6: Inspect Retrieval as Attention-Like Focus ::: {#124c5509 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} query = "cybersecurity and data privacy risk" results = retrieve(query, k=5) score_sum = results["score"].sum() results["attention_like_weight"] = results["score"] / score_sum results[["chunk_id", "company", "item", "score", "attention_like_weight"]] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: The normalized column is not a neural attention weight, but it helps us ask the same question we ask of attention heatmaps: **where is the system focusing, and does that focus make sense for the task?** ## Why This Matters This tutorial gives students the retrieval intuition they need before they start prompt design. It also reinforces an important course habit: - validate retrieval quality before adding generation - inspect what context the model will be allowed to use That same logic carries directly into `M03_Lab1` and later project work. ## AI Use and Share Links {.unnumbered} If generative AI materially supports your work for this tutorial, include an AI disclosure appendix or separate AI disclosure document if your instructor requests one.
